profile.address: 8343, Northeast Evergreen Parkway, Tanasbourne, Hillsboro, Washington County, Oregon, 97124
profile.reading: This Tata Communications facility sits on Northeast Evergreen Parkway in the Tanasbourne area of Hillsboro, Oregon, part of the Portland metro corridor known for chip manufacturing and telecommunications infrastructure. It carries the TGN designation, an abbreviation for the Tata Global Network, the name Tata Communications uses for the wholly owned undersea and terrestrial fiber system it built up around assets originally developed by Tyco Telecommunications. Hillsboro is not a coastal town, so this address most likely functions as an inland cable landing or terminating facility of the kind carriers use to bring a subsea cable's terminated fiber into a secure, road accessible building away from the immediate shoreline, before handing it off into terrestrial backhaul networks reaching Portland and beyond. As with Tata's other cable landing infrastructure, the company does not publish square footage, power capacity, or tenancy information for this specific site. That is consistent with how the submarine cable industry treats individual landing and terminating stations, which are typically described only in aggregate cable system documentation rather than as standalone real estate assets. No county permit or building record specific to this address was found in the course of this research. The facility should be understood as working carrier infrastructure supporting Tata's Pacific network reach, rather than a commercial, multi tenant data center.

reading.body:
TGN Hillsboro is a submarine cable landing station, not a data center with published power capacity, so it contributes no measurable compute or power signal to Oregon's AI infrastructure picture.

The facility sits inland in Hillsboro, Oregon, and functions as carrier network infrastructure for Tata Communications' Tata Global Network, bringing subsea Pacific fiber to a secure location for handoff to terrestrial backhaul. It publishes no square footage, IT load, or tenant information, and no county permits or building records specific to the address were found. That absence is normal for submarine cable landing stations, which carriers document only in aggregate cable system records rather than as standalone real estate.

For AI scaling, the binding constraint is grid power delivered to buildings that house compute. This facility has zero published megawatts and is not a commercial colocation site, so it offers no usable signal for assessing Oregon's AI compute capacity. Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities, but only 8 publish power figures totaling 156.6 MW; TGN Hillsboro's lack of a published figure means it ranks ninth only by default categorization, not by actual capacity, and it should not be counted as evidence of new AI infrastructure.
